title: Cost Model API: add policy guardrails for what-if projections (bounds + allowed ranges)
author: Ethan Park
description: Context: The new Cost Model what-if endpoint is intentionally flexible (batching/caching/quantization knobs) and will be called by Optimize (interactive) and potentially Console (hot paths). In early staging tests and after SUP-31877 triage, we saw two failure modes: (1) callers passing extreme parameter values (e.g., batch size 4096, cache warm-rate > 1.0) leading to unrealistic savings outputs, and (2) expensive computations when callers submit high-cardinality workload summaries (large histograms / too many route keys) that can blow our latency budget and increase tail p95s. This PR adds explicit policy guardrails at the API boundary so the service is safe-by-default, deterministic, and bounded. Summary of changes: (A) Introduce a centralized PolicyGuardrails layer for what-if requests that validates and clamps input ranges (where clamping is explicitly allowed) and rejects invalid/unsafe requests with clear error codes. (B) Enforce request bounds for cardinality: max number of workload segments, max histogram buckets, max distinct route/model keys, and max scenario count per request. (C) Add a compute budget heuristic: estimate worst-case complexity from the request and reject if above threshold (protects CPU and avoids unbounded fanout to model catalog/telemetry lookups). (D) Add an allowlist for parameterized what-if dimensions in v1 (batching, prefix-cache, kv-cache, quant profile change) and explicitly reject unknown/experimental dimensions unless the caller is in an internal allowlist (feature flag + service-to-service identity). (E) Standardize error responses for guardrail failures: HTTP 400 with error_code=CM_GUARDRAIL_* for caller-correctable issues; HTTP 403 for forbidden dimensions/tenancy; HTTP 429 for rate-limit triggers; and a consistent message + remediation hints so Optimize can surface actionable UI text. Guardrails (v1): - scenario_count: max 10 scenarios per request; - workload_segments: max 25 segments (Optimize currently uses <= 8); - histogram buckets: max 32 buckets for seq_len distribution and max 32 for output_len distribution; - route/model keys: max 50 distinct keys; - batch_size_target: [1, 256] (reject outside); - microbatch_size_target: [1, 64]; - cache_hit_rate: [0.0, 1.0] (reject outside; no clamping); - cache_warm_rate: [0.0, 1.0] (reject outside; note: renamed internally to warm_rate to avoid ambiguity); - quantization_profile_id: must exist in model catalog and must be compatible with base model; - overhead_allocation_policy: must be one of {request_attributable_only, blended_cluster_overhead}; - max_estimated_compute_units: 1.0 (internal scale); reject above threshold. Observability: adds metrics cost_model.whatif.guardrail_reject_total{reason=...} and cost_model.whatif.request_shape{segments=...,buckets=...,scenarios=...} to support tuning. Also adds structured log fields guardrail_reason and request_shape_summary for incident triage. Tests: unit tests for validation + error mapping; golden tests ensuring deterministic output and stable error codes; load-test fixture ensuring guardrails prevent worst-case request shapes from entering compute. Notes: This PR intentionally rejects requests rather than silently clamping in most cases, to avoid producing misleading ROI estimates. The only clamping performed is for missing optional fields that have safe defaults (e.g., absent cache_hit_rate defaults to observed baseline). Follow-ups: (1) coordinate with Optimize to align UI input widgets with these ranges and surface error_code messages; (2) document guardrails in internal docs; (3) revisit limits after we collect two weeks of production telemetry on request shapes and latency.

review_conversation: Jonas Weber: Can we avoid clamping at all? It’s dangerous for ROI calculations. Also please ensure we can represent uncertainty later without widening the request shape. Ethan Park: Agreed. The only clamping left is for missing optional baseline fields (safe defaults). Out-of-range values will be rejected with CM_GUARDRAIL_RANGE and a remediation message. Aditya Rao: Optimize uses cache warm-rate in the UI right now. We need a clear contract for warm_rate vs hit_rate, otherwise support issues repeat (SUP-31877). Ethan Park: Added explicit fields warm_rate and hit_rate with bounds [0,1], and updated error messages to call out both. Also rejecting if both are provided but inconsistent with baseline_mode=observed. Sofia Ivanova: The batch_size upper bound of 256 seems low for some offline throughput sweeps, but probably correct for interactive what-if. Can we make it policy-driven per caller? Ethan Park: Implemented per-caller override behind internal allowlist (service identity + flag). Default remains 256 for safety. Rafael Mendes: Please add metrics for rejections and a dashboard-friendly reason label. Also ensure this doesn’t turn into a 5xx for bad input. Ethan Park: Added guardrail_reject_total{reason} and mapped all validation failures to 400 with stable error_code. Allison Grant: Error codes should be stable and documented; also ensure determinism (same input => same error). Ethan Park: Added error catalog in schema package and golden tests asserting exact error_code strings. Requested changes (round 1): tighten defaults, add tests for worst-case request shape, and include allowlist behavior. Addressed in commits 4-6. Approvals: Jonas, Sofia, Rafael, Allison, Aditya.
